result: The authors demonstrate that p73α to p73γ isoform switching occurs in human cancers and dog lymphomas. Analysis of TCGA data shows increased exon 11 exclusion in lung and head-neck squamous cell carcinomas compared to normal tissues (C26, C27). In human prostate carcinomas, p73α is lost while p73γ is elevated compared to normal prostates (C28, C29). Similarly, in dog lymphomas, p73α is undetectable while p73γ is elevated compared to normal lymph nodes (C31, C32).
evaluation: Claims C26-C32 provide converging evidence from multiple tissue types (human lung, head-neck, prostate cancers and dog lymphomas) showing consistent p73α to p73γ isoform switching. The data includes both bioinformatic analysis (TCGA) and experimental measurements (RT-PCR) with appropriate controls (normal tissues). Sample sizes appear adequate (n=5 normal prostates, n=16 prostate carcinomas; n=3 normal lymph nodes, n=16 lymphomas).

result: CRISPR-mediated deletion of the E11 splicing acceptor in TP73 successfully triggers exon 11 skipping and results in isoform switching from p73α to p73γ. E11-KO cells show loss of α/β isoforms, increased γ/ε isoforms, and unchanged δ/ζ isoforms compared to isogenic controls (C34). TA/ΔNp73 isoforms remain at similar levels (C35), and TAp73γ becomes the predominant isoform in E11-KO cells while TAp73α is predominant in controls (C36).
evaluation: Claims C33-C36 demonstrate successful genetic manipulation to model the isoform switch observed in cancers. The experimental design is sound with appropriate isogenic controls, and multiple detection methods (RT-PCR, Western blot with specific antibodies) confirm the isoform switch at both transcript and protein levels. The data in Figure 2A-C support these claims.

result: E11 deficiency promotes oncogenic phenotypes in vitro. E11-KO cells show enhanced colony formation compared to TAp73-KO cells (C37-C39), increased cell migration compared to all other cell lines including TAp73-KO (C40-C43), and aberrant epithelial morphogenesis with irregular acini and filled lumen similar to TAp73-KO cells (C46).
evaluation: Claims C37-C43, C46 are well-supported by multiple complementary assays (colony formation, scratch assay, transwell migration, 3D culture) across multiple cell lines (H1299, Mia-PaCa2, MCF10A). The inclusion of TAp73-KO, ΔNp73-KO, and isogenic controls allows proper comparison. The finding that E11-KO shows stronger oncogenic effects than TAp73-KO is particularly notable and well-documented.

result: TAp73γ is primarily responsible for the oncogenic effects observed in E11-KO cells. Inducible expression of TAp73γ promotes cell migration (C47). Knockdown of p73α/γ has opposite effects in control versus E11-KO cells: it enhances migration and tumor sphere viability in controls but decreases them in E11-KO cells (C48-C50). ΔNp73/E11 double knockout does not alter migration compared to E11-KO alone (C51), indicating TAp73γ can overcome ΔNp73 deficiency effects (C52).
evaluation: Claims C47-C52, C110 provide strong evidence through gain-of-function (inducible TAp73γ) and loss-of-function (siRNA knockdown, double knockout) approaches. The opposite effects of p73α/γ knockdown in control versus E11-KO cells elegantly demonstrate that p73α (predominant in controls) suppresses while p73γ (predominant in E11-KO) promotes oncogenic phenotypes. The double knockout experiment (C51) provides additional genetic evidence.

result: E11-deficient mice recapitulate key phenotypes of Trp73-deficient mice but show distinct tumor spectrum. E11 deficiency causes isoform switching in MEFs (C53), reduced cellular senescence (C54), and in E11-KO mice causes runty phenotype, infertility, and hydrocephalus (C55). E11-HET mice show shortened lifespan similar to Trp73+/- mice (C56), increased tumor incidence (C57), but significantly higher percentage of DLBCL (50% vs 14.8%) (C58). Both genotypes show chronic inflammation (C59-C60) and various hyperplasias (C61-C64), though with some differences in severity and tissue distribution.
evaluation: Claims C53-C64, C111 are supported by comprehensive in vivo analysis with adequate sample sizes (n=51 WT, n=27 Trp73+/-, n=28 E11-HET mice). Statistical analysis is appropriate (Fisher's exact test, log-rank test). The finding that E11-HET mice show higher DLBCL incidence than Trp73+/- mice (p=0.009) is particularly significant and suggests a specific role for p73γ in B-cell lymphomagenesis. However, the use of historical controls for WT and some Trp73+/- mice is a limitation.

result: E11 deficiency leads to obesity and altered lipid metabolism. E11-HET mice show enlarged adipocytes (C65), increased VAT mass (C66), liver steatosis (C67), elevated liver enzyme transcripts (C68), and increased serum cholesterol and triglycerides at both old (~65 weeks) and young (20-32 weeks) ages (C69-C72). In vitro, E11-KO cells show increased cholesterol and triglycerides that is reversed by p73γ knockdown (C73-C74), while p73α/γ knockdown in control cells increases lipid levels (C75).
evaluation: Claims C65-C75 provide strong evidence through multiple complementary approaches (histology, serum measurements, in vitro assays) with appropriate controls. The in vitro rescue experiments (C74) and the opposite effect of knockdown in control cells (C75) strengthen the conclusion that p73γ promotes while p73α inhibits lipid storage. Sample sizes appear adequate (n=3 per group for most measurements). The phenotype is observed at multiple ages, suggesting it is not merely age-related.

result: Leptin is a direct transcriptional target of p73 isoforms, with strongest induction by TAp73γ. E11-HET mice show adipose tissue inflammation (C76), increased proinflammatory cytokines (C77), and elevated Leptin in tissues and serum (C78-C81). Leptin expression is markedly increased in E11-HET compared to Trp73+/- mice (C82). In cells, TAp73 and E11-KO increase Leptin while ΔNp73-KO has little effect (C83-C85). Ectopic TAp73γ induces Leptin (C86, C89), while p73γ knockdown reduces it in E11-KO cells (C87). Both p73α and p73γ can regulate Leptin, with p73γ being strongest (C88-C89, C108).
evaluation: Claims C76-C89, C108 establish Leptin as a p73 target through multiple lines of evidence: correlation in vivo (C76-C82), genetic manipulation in cells (C83-C89), and the claim of direct targeting (C108) is supported by subsequent mechanistic studies (C90-C94). The dose-response relationship (E11-HET > Trp73+/- > WT) and the differential effects of p73 isoforms are well-documented. However, C108 requires additional mechanistic evidence from subsequent claims to be fully supported.

result: Leptin is a direct transcriptional target of TAp73 through a specific p73 response element. A putative p73-RE is located at nt -346 to -321 in the Leptin promoter (C90). ChIP assays demonstrate that both ectopic TAp73γ (C91) and endogenous p73γ in E11-KO cells (C92) bind to the Leptin promoter. Luciferase reporter assays show that TAp73α/β/γ activate the wild-type Leptin promoter, with strongest activation by TAp73γ (C93), but cannot activate a reporter with mutant p73-RE (C94).
evaluation: Claims C90-C94 provide strong mechanistic evidence for direct transcriptional regulation through complementary approaches: bioinformatic identification of the response element (C90), ChIP assays demonstrating binding (C91-C92), and functional validation through luciferase assays (C93-C94). The mutation of the p73-RE abolishing transactivation (C94) is particularly strong evidence for specificity. These claims together support the conclusion that Leptin is a direct target.

result: Leptin mediates the oncogenic effects of TAp73γ. Knockdown of Leptin abolishes the elevated cholesterol/triglycerides (C95) and enhanced cell migration (C96-C97) caused by E11-KO. LepR is expressed at similar levels across cell lines (C98), and exogenous Leptin treatment enhances cell transmigration (C99). In human prostate carcinomas and dog lymphomas, Leptin expression correlates with p73γ expression (C100-C101).
evaluation: Claims C95-C101 demonstrate that Leptin is functionally important for p73γ-mediated effects through loss-of-function (siRNA) and gain-of-function (exogenous Leptin) approaches. The correlation between Leptin and p73γ in clinical samples (C100-C101) provides translational relevance. The finding that LepR is not regulated by p73 (C98) is important for interpreting the Leptin treatment experiments. The data support Leptin as a critical mediator.

result: Targeting p73γ or Leptin suppresses E11-KO xenograft tumor growth. E11-KO cells form larger tumors than control cells (C102-C103) with elevated p73γ and Leptin (C104). Intratumoral injection of siRNAs against p73γ or Leptin significantly reduces tumor growth rate (C105), tumor size and weight (C106), and causes extensive tumor necrosis (C107).
evaluation: Claims C102-C107 provide strong in vivo validation of therapeutic potential. The experimental design includes appropriate controls (scrambled siRNA) and adequate sample sizes (n=6-7 per group). Statistical significance is demonstrated (p<0.05). The extensive tumor necrosis (C107) is a particularly striking phenotype. However, the use of transient transfection followed by injection and one additional intratumoral injection may not fully represent sustained knockdown, which is a limitation for therapeutic interpretation.

result: The authors propose that p73α and p73γ have opposing functions in tumorigenesis, and that the p73γ-Leptin pathway promotes tumorigenesis and alters lipid metabolism. This represents a novel paradigm where C-terminal p73 isoforms (p73α vs p73γ) have opposing roles similar to N-terminal isoforms (TAp73 vs ΔNp73).
evaluation: Claims C109 and C112 represent the major conclusions synthesized from all experimental results. The evidence from multiple experimental systems (cell lines, mouse models, clinical samples) consistently shows that p73α suppresses while p73γ promotes oncogenic phenotypes, lipid accumulation, and Leptin expression. The mechanistic link through Leptin is well-established. These conclusions are well-supported by the totality of the data, though they represent interpretive synthesis rather than single experimental findings.

result: The authors provide comprehensive background on TP73 gene structure, p73 isoforms, and their known functions. This includes chromosomal location (C1), similarity to p53 (C2-C3), mutation frequency (C4), biological functions (C5), promoter usage generating TA and ΔN isoforms (C6-C8), mouse phenotypes (C9-C10), context-dependent activities (C11), and C-terminal splicing variants (C12-C18).
evaluation: Claims C1-C18 are background information supported by appropriate citations to published literature. These establish the scientific context for the study but do not represent new findings. The claims accurately represent established knowledge about p73 biology based on the citations provided.

result: The authors provide background on Leptin biology, including its structure and production (C19), role in energy homeostasis (C20), anti-obesity effects in congenital deficiency (C21), leptin resistance in common obesity (C22), pleiotropic functions (C23), role in cancer progression (C24), and alterations in obesity-associated cancers (C25).
evaluation: Claims C19-C25 are background information supported by appropriate citations to published literature. These establish the rationale for investigating Leptin as a potential mediator of p73γ effects but do not represent new findings. The claims accurately represent established knowledge about Leptin biology.

result: In 3D culture, parental and isogenic control MCF10A cells form normal acini with hollow lumen (C44), while ΔNp73-KO cells show delayed acinus formation with small acini (C45).
evaluation: Claims C44-C45 are supported by the 3D culture data in Figure 2G. These serve as controls for the E11-KO and TAp73-KO phenotypes (C46) and demonstrate that ΔNp73 has a distinct role in epithelial morphogenesis. The data are clear and appropriately controlled.
